subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 44-year-old man with a 15-year history of heavy alcohol use reports 2 months of numbness and burning of both feet that has spread to the shins, along with weakness that makes him trip. Examination shows symmetric distal weakness with foot drop, wasting of the intrinsic hand muscles, absent ankle reflexes, and stocking-glove sensory loss. Serum glucose, vitamin B12, and folate levels are normal.
question: Which of the following laboratory studies would best confirm the diagnosis?

options.text: Increase in erythrocyte transketolase activity after administration of thiamine

explanation_correct: This patient has dry beriberi, the neurologic form of thiamine deficiency, which produces a symmetric sensorimotor polyneuropathy with distal muscle wasting and areflexia. Thiamine deficiency is confirmed by an increase in erythrocyte transketolase activity after vitamin B1 administration, because transketolase is a thiamine pyrophosphate-dependent enzyme. Transketolase activity also falls in the red cells of these patients even before structural nerve damage becomes irreversible.

explanation_incorrect.A: Methylmalonic acid rises in vitamin B12 deficiency, which this patient's normal B12 level and the absence of megaloblastic anemia make unlikely.
explanation_incorrect.B: Vitamin E deficiency can cause a posterior column and spinocerebellar syndrome, but it occurs with fat malabsorption and does not explain symmetric distal wasting with alcohol use.
explanation_incorrect.C: Parietal cell antibodies are used to evaluate pernicious anemia (vitamin B12 deficiency), which is excluded by the normal B12 level.
explanation_incorrect.E: Urinary porphobilinogen evaluates acute intermittent porphyria, which produces episodic abdominal pain and neurovisceral attacks rather than a chronic distally symmetric neuropathy.

educationalObjective: Dry beriberi is a thiamine deficiency polyneuropathy with symmetric distal wasting, and the diagnosis is supported by increased erythrocyte transketolase activity after thiamine administration.
